newsitem.title: UK: Soccer can hurt fertility - Italian scientists.
newsitem.headline: Soccer can hurt fertility - Italian scientists.

text.p: Young soccer players who train hard risk damaging their manhood and even becoming infertile, Italian researchers warned on Friday.

Dr Andrea Scaramuzza, a team doctor for Milan AC, and colleagues at the University of Pavia told the Lancet medical journal they found that adolescent soccer players were prone to smaller testicles and varicocele, a painless condition of the testicles.
Varicoceles are varicose veins around the spermatic cord, which takes sperm from the testicle. It causes no symptoms but affects blood supply to the testes and can lead to infertility.

Scaramuzza's group studied 198 boys aged 10 to 14 and found that none of the boys who did not train had the problem. But 30 percent of the boys who trained for 10 or more hours a week had varicoceles.
"Sports training might cause varicocele by some mechanical effect of exercise," the researchers suggested in a letter to the Lancet. Theyadvised that young athletes be regularly examined.
